title: Sign in with Google from the web app
description:
**Phase 3 of 7.**

- **Blocked by:** 0df6cb
- **Runs in parallel with:** 5f0c4c, fac2ee, 41d08d, and 79578e
- **Unblocks:** 22f5bb

---
oidc-client-ts doing authorization code with PKCE against the Cognito app client, with identity_provider=Google on the authorize URL so Cognito's own page never renders and the person goes straight to Google. Tokens live in memory with silent renew, not in localStorage.

web/next.config.ts is output: export, so there is no Node runtime in the web tier and no server-side session. That is why the relying party is Cognito and the token is a bearer, not a cookie. web/lib/sse.ts already uses fetch rather than EventSource so it can send headers, so a bearer token needs no transport change.

**Done when:** a person signs in against development and the app holds a verified token.

comments.text:
summary: Sign in with Google from the web app is live and complete on development. The web SPA signs in via oidc-client-ts using authorization code + PKCE against the Cognito app client with identity_provider=Google on the authorize URL (Cognito's own page never renders; the person goes straight to Google), holding a verified id_token in memory with silent renew — no localStorage, no server-side session, no cookie; the token is a bearer sent via fetch headers in web/lib/sse.ts.

Landed across four PRs: #157 wired the SPA PKCE flow, in-memory id_token, identity_provider=Google, and the viewer-request /auth/callback rewrite for the trailingSlash export; #159 made BucketDeployment not block on CloudFront invalidation confirm (CDK issue 15891) so named ChatticusWeb deploys succeed; #160 switched NEXT_PUBLIC_* Cognito config to static build-time access (Next does not inline dynamic process.env[name]) so the bundle carries pool id, auth-dev.chattic.us, and the callback URL; #161 set the oidc-client-ts authority to the cognito-idp issuer (discovery lives at cognito-idp/{userPoolId}, not the custom domain which 404s). Each was followed by a named ChatticusWeb development redeploy.

End-to-end sign-in was then blocked by Cognito reporting email_verified=false on Google id_tokens; #165 mapped ProviderAttribute.GOOGLE_EMAIL_VERIFIED into the id_token (part of 0df6cb's follow-through), after which GET /me returns 200 and the app holds a verified token. The human owner has signed in to https://dev.chattic.us via Google many times since, including through the membership branching work (22f5bb). Done-when met: a person signs in against development and the app holds a verified token. Closing.
